config.title: Test User Interactions

intro.title: Test User Interactions
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple interactive form component and learn how to test user interactions like typing and clicking. You'll use Vue's reactive data properties to manage form state and Vue Test Utils to simulate user actions in a test environment. The core concept is writing unit tests that verify your component responds correctly to user input, ensuring your UI behaves as expected. You'll work with Vue components, Jest or Vitest for testing, and event handling to create a reliable, test-driven user interface.
intro.usecase: Testing user interactions is essential for ensuring that interactive components in real applications behave correctly. In e-commerce sites, you need to verify that product filters update search results when users click category buttons or adjust price sliders. For SaaS dashboards, you must test that data visualizations respond properly when users toggle between different time periods or metric views. Form validation testing ensures that error messages appear appropriately when users submit incomplete information, while modal interactions confirm that overlays open and close as expected during user workflows.

objectives: Initialize a Vue component with reactive state for user interaction testing
Implement event handlers to capture user inputs in Vue components
Bind form elements to Vue's reactive data model for two-way data flow
Render dynamic UI elements based on user interaction state
Configure Vue event modifiers to control event behavior in tests
Integrate user interaction logic with component methods for test scenarios
Manipulate DOM elements programmatically to simulate user actions in tests

steps.title: Import Vue and testing utilities
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the testing utilities (mount, flushPromises) from the appropriate packages. Add these imports at the top of your file.
steps.hint: You'll need to import Vue from 'vue' and mount/flushPromises from '@vue/test-utils'.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue and testing utilities here

// Your component code will go below
steps.expectedOutcome: The file will have the necessary imports for Vue and testing utilities at the top.
successCriteria: Vue is imported from 'vue' and mount/flushPromises are imported from '@vue/test-utils'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both Vue from 'vue' and mount/flushPromises from '@vue/test-utils'.
steps.feedbackWrong: import Vue from 'vue' and mount/flushPromises from '@vue/test-utils' for testing user interactions.

steps.title: Create a basic Vue component for testing
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named 'InteractiveComponent' that returns a template with a single <div> wrapper containing a heading that says 'Test User Interactions'.
steps.hint: Define a component using Vue's defineComponent or a simple object with a template property. The template should contain a <div> with an <h1> inside.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Vue component named 'InteractiveComponent' is defined with a template containing a heading inside a div wrapper.
successCriteria: The component is named 'InteractiveComponent' and has a template with a <div> containing an <h1> with the text 'Test User Interactions'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your component is named 'InteractiveComponent' and includes the heading text exactly as specified.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't match the requirements. Check that you've named it 'InteractiveComponent' and included the correct heading text in the template.

steps.title: Add reactive data to the component
steps.instruction: Inside your component, add a data function that returns an object with a reactive property named 'count' initialized to 0.
steps.hint: In Vue, reactive data is defined in the data option as a function returning an object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has reactive data that can be used for testing user interactions.
successCriteria: Component has a data function returning an object with a 'count' property set to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your data function returns an object with exactly 'count: 0'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component needs a data function that returns { count: 0 }. Check the syntax for Vue's data option.

steps.title: Define a method to handle user interaction
steps.instruction: Add a methods object to your component with a function named handleClick that increments the count property by 1.
steps.hint: In Vue, methods are defined as an object within the component options. Each method is a function that can access reactive data using 'this'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a handleClick method that increases the count when called, preparing it for user interaction testing.
successCriteria: A methods object is added to the component with a handleClick function that increments this.count.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a methods object, but make sure it contains a handleClick function that increments this.count by 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: The methods object or handleClick function is missing or incorrect. Check that you've added the methods object with a proper function that modifies the count data.

steps.title: Add interactive elements to the template
steps.instruction: Add a template section to your component with a button element that displays 'Increment' as its text.
steps.hint: In Vue single-file components, you need to add a <template> section. Inside it, create a <button> element with the text 'Increment'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button to a template
<template>
  <button>Click me</button>
</template>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a template section containing a button with the text 'Increment'.
successCriteria: A <template> section is added with a <button> element containing the text 'Increment'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a <template> section with a <button> element that says 'Increment'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template or button isn't correctly added. Check that you have a <template> section with a <button> element containing 'Increment' text.

steps.title: Wire the interactive elements to the method
steps.instruction: Add click event handlers to the buttons that call the increment method you defined earlier.
steps.hint: Use the @click directive on each button element to call the increment method.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: wiring a button to a method
<button @click="increment">Add</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The buttons will have click handlers that call the increment method when clicked.
successCriteria: Both buttons have @click event handlers that call the increment method.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some event handlers, but make sure both buttons have @click handlers that call the increment method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons don't have the correct event handlers. Use @click to call the increment method on both buttons.

steps.title: Display the reactive data in the template
steps.instruction: Update the paragraph in the template to show 'Current count: ' followed by the count value.
steps.hint: Use template interpolation with double curly braces to display the count data property.
steps.analogousExample: // Displaying reactive data in a template
steps.expectedOutcome: The paragraph will display the current count value with a descriptive prefix.
successCriteria: The paragraph shows 'Current count: ' followed by the count value using template interpolation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using template interpolation ({{ count }}) and adding the 'Current count: ' prefix.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph should display 'Current count: ' followed by the count value using template interpolation.

steps.title: Create a test file and import dependencies
steps.instruction: Create a new test file named 'Counter.test.js' and import the component and testing utilities.
steps.hint: Start by creating a new file in your project. Use import statements to bring in the component and testing utilities you'll need for testing.
steps.seedCode:
// Create a new file named Counter.test.js
// Import the component and testing utilities here
steps.expectedOutcome: A test file is created with the necessary imports for testing the Counter component.
successCriteria: Counter.test.js file exists with imports for the Counter component and Vue Test Utils.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the test file, but make sure to import both the Counter component and the testing utilities from Vue Test Utils.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test file setup is incomplete. Create Counter.test.js and import the Counter component along with testing utilities like mount from '@vue/test-utils'.

steps.title: Write a test to mount the component
steps.instruction: In Counter.test.js, write a test that mounts the Counter component using the imported mount function. The test should verify the component renders correctly.
steps.hint: Use the mount function to render the Counter component inside a test block.
steps.expectedOutcome: A test that mounts the Counter component and checks it exists.
successCriteria: The test uses mount to render the Counter component and includes an assertion.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the mount function and have an assertion to verify the component renders.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test doesn't mount the Counter component correctly. Check that you're using the mount function and have a proper test structure.

steps.title: Write a test to simulate user interaction
steps.instruction: Inside the describe block, write a test that simulates a button click and asserts the counter value increases.
steps.hint: Use wrapper.find() to locate the button, then .trigger('click') to simulate a click. Check the updated text with .text().
steps.expectedOutcome: The test file will contain a test case that simulates clicking the button and verifies the counter updates correctly.
successCriteria: Test case includes button click simulation and assertion for updated counter value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your test includes both the button click simulation and an assertion about the counter value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test doesn't properly simulate user interaction. Check that you're finding the button, triggering a click, and asserting the expected result.
